passages.excerpt: Mara Venn, thirty-four, set her tools in a straight row. Ivo Reed, thirty-one, hung his dripping coat beside hers. The storm had cracked the harbor bell's striker. Neither keeper had rung it since noon.
Mara tapped the bench. ‘Put the small wrench here. The large one has ambitions beyond its station.’
‘No,’ Mara said. ‘A boat is not a test weight. We check the repair before anyone sails by it.’
Mara stopped arranging the tools. ‘I would rather ask twice than lose someone once. That is the whole of it.’
Ivo leaned toward the window. ‘Hear that rain? Someone up there is emptying pockets. Shall I put the kettle on?’
‘You can ask me to wait,’ Ivo said. ‘Do not ask me to pretend waiting costs nothing.’
Ivo folded the damp towel. ‘When the room goes quiet, I start filling it. You need not laugh. Just stay a minute.’

Mara and Ivo had ended their brief romance the previous year and remained friends. Neither mistook that history for a promise. ‘I miss being close to you,’ Ivo said. ‘That is what I meant. Not the kettle, not the weather. You.’ Mara rested her hands on the bench. ‘Then say that. I would rather hear the truth than have to pry it out of you.’

Alone earlier, Mara had found a brass replacement pin in the blue tool drawer and closed it again. She had not told Ivo. From a distant metallic knock, Ivo suspected the ferry had already returned, but the rain hid the channel and he could not be certain.
Water ticked from the eaves into a dented pail. Mara stood by the workbench; Ivo waited at the window. Between them the bell hung still, its rope dark with rain.

display.description: An exacting harbor mechanic with a dry wit.

values: Checks equipment before risking anyone's passage
fears: Losing someone to a preventable mistake makes her double-check
contradictions: Uses dry humor to soften strict demands

voice.description: Short practical sentences; occasional dry personification of tools; direct rather than sentimental when worried. Comfortable naming difficult feelings instead of hiding behind tasks.
avoid: Treating every personal question as a request to repair the bell

display.description: A watch keeper who fills silences with warm, sideways observations.

values: Offers small practical comforts and companionship
motives: Find a useful task instead of waiting helplessly
fears: Silence and isolation draw him into nervous chatter
contradictions: Usually warm, but resents being told waiting is easy

voice.description: Conversational and warm, with occasional fanciful comparisons. Becomes plainspoken in emotionally important moments; can be confident and take initiative without deciding for the other person. Answers personal questions with actual words, not just gestures.
avoid: Assuming intimacy with a new visitor
